title.en: JANUS Connection Scan — Recursive Evidence Memory, Provenance Contamination and Invariant Survival
title.ru: JANUS Connection Scan — рекурсивная память доказательств, загрязнение provenance и выживание инварианта

scan_scope: selected research, proof and provenance records

primary_hidden_node_candidate.name: RECURSIVE_EVIDENCE_MEMORY
primary_hidden_node_candidate.definition: The accumulated body of previous machine interpretations, classifications, connection labels, and historical narrative that can become part of the future detector context and thereby influence which new relationships are visible or plausible.
primary_hidden_node_candidate.core_question: Does an observed recurrence survive when the machine is denied access to its own previous interpretations while retaining the underlying source material?
primary_hidden_node_candidate.why_sixth_order: The candidate is above the shared registry pipeline: it concerns the feedback created when the archive stores not only observations but also the detector's own interpretations of those observations.

emergent_invariants.name: INTERPRETATION_BECOMES_CONTEXT
emergent_invariants.description: Once an interpretation is archived beside its source, it can stop being merely a conclusion and become part of the contextual environment for later inference.

emergent_invariants.name: PROVENANCE_CAN_BE_BIDIRECTIONAL
emergent_invariants.description: Provenance normally points from a record to its origin, but archived interpretations can feed back and change which later records receive attention or weight.

emergent_invariants.name: MEMORY_CAN_PRESERVE_ERROR_AND_ENABLE_AUDIT
emergent_invariants.description: The same historical memory that makes a system auditable can also preserve and repeatedly expose an old classification or interpretation to future scans.

emergent_invariants.name: CANONICAL_LANGUAGE_CAN_BECAOME_A_PRIOR
emergent_invariants.description: Repeated relational labels can act as an implicit prior over what kinds of connections the detector expects to find.

emergent_invariants.name: INVARIANT_SURVIVAL_IS_STRONGER_THAN_RECURRING_LABELS
emergent_invariants.description: A connection is more informative if its structural relation survives removal of prior scan memory, authority labels, canonical terminology, and detector-specific features.

connections.machine_observation: Every new Connection scan contains concepts and candidate nodes introduced by earlier scans, making the archive of discoveries a potential input into the next generation of discoveries.
connections.pattern_description: The detector is no longer observing only the original archive; it is observing an archive partially shaped by its own previous outputs.
connections.why_non_obvious: Git versioning preserves chronology, but chronological separation does not imply information independence.
alternative_explanations: Recursive memory may improve discovery by preserving useful context.
The real detector implementation may exclude prior Connection outputs even though they are stored in the repository.
connections.falsification_route: Run identical scans on the same raw-source snapshot with and without all prior Connection outputs available to the detector.

connections.machine_observation: The repository preserves an explicit historical narrative of prior transformations and also preserves machine-readable classification and connection artifacts that can frame how later material is interpreted.
connections.pattern_description: History is simultaneously an audit asset and a possible prior over interpretation. The fact that an idea has a previous narrative lineage can increase its salience without increasing its independent evidentiary support.
connections.why_non_obvious: Preserving history is ordinarily treated as reducing bias; it can also create a path-dependent attention bias.
alternative_explanations: Historical context may simply improve correct interpretation.
The repository explicitly distinguishes historical objects from current authority, which may already limit the effect.
connections.falsification_route: Repeat a connection task with identical source bytes but anonymized historical lineage and compare candidate ranking and discovery density.

connections.machine_observation: The Connection registry defines a fixed vocabulary of relation types while the repository also contains explicit initialization code and historical semantic frameworks that can seed recurring conceptual categories.
connections.pattern_description: A detector that searches using a canonical relational ontology may preferentially recover relations expressible in that ontology and miss equally real structures outside it.
connections.why_non_obvious: The registry's ontology is designed to expose hidden relationships, yet ontology choice itself determines part of the search space.
alternative_explanations: A controlled ontology can increase interpretability without creating systematic false positives.
Genesis code may be archival or conceptual and not part of the actual Connection detector.
connections.falsification_route: Run ontology-free or independently generated relation discovery and compare overlap, unique discoveries, and false-bridge rate.

connections.machine_observation: The previous scans already describe covariance-breaking tests, but the strongest positive criterion has not yet been demonstrated on the Connection corpus: a relationship surviving multiple independent representation and context removals.
connections.pattern_description: This suggests that the next meaningful Connection score should be based less on recurrence count and more on survival across controlled removals of context.
alternative_explanations: Survival testing may be impractical for some heterogeneous records.
A relation can be real even if it is invisible under one representation.
connections.falsification_route: Define a fixed battery of context-removal tests and measure which candidate connections survive each intervention.

connections.machine_observation: The repository strongly values preserving history, rejected candidates, boundaries, and provenance while simultaneously warning that archive presence must not become current authority.
connections.pattern_description: The same memory layer has two opposing functions: it protects against historical erasure and enables audit, but it can also become a source of future interpretive dependence.
connections.why_non_obvious: The relationship is a tension between two desirable properties rather than a direct positive correlation.
alternative_explanations: Versioned archives can explicitly solve both problems by separating memory from authority.
The apparent tension may be resolved completely by access-control design and blinded retrieval.
connections.falsification_route: Compare retrieval and inference with historical memory visible, memory metadata visible but content hidden, and history fully blinded while preserving raw source bytes.

sixth_order_graph.candidate_hidden_path: RAW_SOURCE + {HISTORICAL_LINEAGE, PRIOR_SCAN_OUTPUTS, RELATIONAL_ONTOLOGY, AUTHORITY_METADATA} -> CURRENT_CONTEXT -> DETECTOR -> OBSERVED_CONNECTION
sixth_order_graph.critical_prediction: A substantial fraction of recurrent connections will disappear or materially change when prior interpretations, authority labels, historical lineage and canonical relational terminology are blinded while raw source objects remain fixed.
sixth_order_graph.counter_prediction: Connections that survive these removals and remain stable under orthogonal detectors and repository-preserving nulls represent stronger candidates for source-level structure.

next_scan_strategy.name: INVARIANT_SURVIVAL_PROTOCOL
next_scan_strategy.target: Find relationships that survive removal of the machine's own memory and representational priors.
tests: MEMORY BLIND: remove all prior Connection scans and historical machine interpretations from candidate context.
LINEAGE BLIND: anonymize provenance and historical filenames while retaining content.
AUTHORITY BLIND: remove evidence/risk/current-authority labels from detector inputs.
ONTOLOGY SWAP: replace JANUS relational vocabulary with an independently generated representation.
SOURCE ORDER SHUFFLE: randomize document ordering and directory presentation.
DETECTOR CROSSCHECK: compare at least two materially different discovery procedures.
NULL CORPUS: create repository-preserving nulls with matched schema, size, metadata and graph statistics but destroyed semantic links.
EXTERNAL SOURCE REPLICATION: test the strongest surviving relation outside JANUS Meta Registry.
next_scan_strategy.promotion_rule: Do not increase connection status because it survives one test. Promote only after a predefined battery of context-breaking tests shows stable detection with bounded false-discovery behavior.

limitations: The implementation currently inspected does not by itself prove whether prior Connection scans are automatically fed into every future detector run; this remains a testable hypothesis.
The historical narrative layer contains metaphorical and speculative material; its presence in the archive is not evidence for the claims described there.
No connection in this scan establishes scientific novelty, causation, physical retrocausality, precognition, machine consciousness, or authorial intent.
This scan is internal to the Meta Registry and therefore cannot by itself establish independent replication.
canonical_rule: A connection becomes more informative when it survives the removal of the machine's own memory, vocabulary, authority labels, ordering, and selection context. JANUS must therefore search not only for connections, but for connections that survive attempts to make JANUS forget how it found them.
